title: GTA 6's Biggest Competition: Ananta Coming to PC in 2027
description: NetEase's anime-style open-world game Ananta has officially scheduled its PC release for early 2027, strategically avoiding Rockstar's GTA 6.
author: GTA6 Hub Editorial
content:
## NetEase's Anime GTA 'Ananta' Targets Early 2027 PC Release

As Rockstar Games' highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto 6 continues to dominate industry discussions, other publishers are carefully planning their release strategies to avoid getting overshadowed. According to a recent report by gaming media outlet Polygon, NetEase's open-world project *Ananta*—often dubbed by fans and observers as the "anime GTA"—is officially slated for a PC release in early 2027.

This strategic release window is viewed by industry analysts as a smart move to steer clear of the massive market shockwave expected from *GTA 6*. By carving out a distinct space in early 2027, *Ananta* aims to attract players who are looking for a massive open-world experience infused with anime aesthetics and unique gameplay mechanics, without having to directly compete in the same release timeframe.

## What to Expect from the PC Launch

While *GTA 6* remains the undisputed giant of the open-world genre, projects like *Ananta* demonstrate how developers are attempting to capture different segments of the gaming audience through stylistic differentiation. The early 2027 release date gives the development team ample time to polish the PC version, ensuring that the anime-inspired world delivers a smooth and engaging experience for players.

As we get closer to 2027, more details regarding gameplay mechanics, system requirements, and exact launch schedules are expected to emerge. It will be fascinating to see how this stylistic alternative fares in a market heavily influenced by Rockstar's juggernaut.

## Editor's Take
Scheduling *Ananta* for early 2027 is a clever strategy. Trying to go head-to-head with *GTA 6* is a daunting task for any title, so leaning into a distinct anime open-world style while avoiding the same release window gives NetEase's project a much better fighting chance in the current market.
